exercises.video_explanation_script: The close-grip bench press is the king of compound tricep exercises. Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell with your hands about 8 to 12 inches apart - that's closer than a regular bench press but not so narrow that your hands are touching. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms extended. Lower the bar to your lower chest or upper abdomen, keeping your elbows tucked at about 45 degrees from your body - don't let them flare out wide. Once the bar touches your chest, press it back up, thinking about pushing it slightly back toward your face. Lock out fully at the top and squeeze your triceps. This exercise allows you to use heavy weight and builds serious tricep mass and strength.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Overhead tricep extensions are the best exercise for targeting the long head of your triceps. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, cupping the top plate, and extend your arms straight up overhead. Your elbows should be pointing forward and close to your head. From here, lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms completely still - only your forearms move. Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your triceps. Then press the dumbbell back up overhead, fully extending your arms and squeezing your triceps at the top. The key is keeping your elbows pointing forward and not letting them flare out to the sides. The overhead position puts the long head under maximum stretch, which is crucial for building tricep mass.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Cable tricep pushdowns are a staple exercise for building triceps. Set a cable pulley to the highest position and attach a straight bar or V-bar. Stand facing the machine with a slight forward lean and grab the bar with an overhand grip. Start with your elbows tucked at your sides and bent about 90 degrees. From here, push the bar straight down by extending your elbows, keeping your upper arms completely still. Fully extend your arms at the bottom and squeeze your triceps hard. Control the cable back up to the starting position. The key is keeping your elbows pinned at your sides - they shouldn't move forward or back. The constant tension from the cable makes this excellent for really feeling your triceps work.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Dips are one of the best compound exercises for building triceps and chest. Grab parallel dip bars and support yourself with arms fully extended - this is your starting position. Keep your shoulders down, not shrugged up. With a slight forward lean, lower yourself down by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows tracking back, not flaring out too wide. Descend until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor - don't go deeper than that or you'll stress your shoulders. From the bottom, press yourself back up to full arm extension, squeezing your triceps at the top. The key is controlling the descent and fully locking out at the top. Once you can do 10+ reps with bodyweight, add weight with a dip belt to continue progressing.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Skull crushers, also called lying tricep extensions, are a classic mass-building tricep exercise. Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with your arms extended above your upper chest. Your hands should be closer than shoulder-width apart. Here's the key: keep your upper arms in this position - they don't move. Lower the bar toward your forehead or just past the top of your head by bending your elbows. Control this descent carefully - hence the name 'skull crusher.' Feel the stretch in your triceps at the bottom. Then press the bar back up by extending your elbows, fully locking out at the top. Only your forearms move, your upper arms stay in position. Use an EZ-bar if possible as it's easier on your wrists than a straight bar.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Diamond push-ups are the most effective bodyweight exercise for building triceps. Get into a push-up position, but bring your hands close together under your chest so your index fingers and thumbs form a diamond or triangle shape. Your body should be in a straight line from head to heels - engage your core to maintain this plank position. Lower yourself down by bending your elbows, keeping them tucked close to your sides. Descend until your chest nearly touches your hands. Then press yourself back up, fully extending your arms and squeezing your triceps at the top. The close hand position puts maximum emphasis on your triceps. If regular diamond push-ups are too difficult, start with your hands on an elevated surface or drop to your knees.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Cable rope overhead extensions are excellent for targeting the long head of your triceps with constant tension. Set a cable pulley to the lowest position and attach a rope. Face away from the machine and grab the rope ends. Step forward and bring the rope overhead so it's behind your head with your elbows bent. Your upper arms should be close to your head, elbows pointing forward. From here, press the rope up and forward overhead by extending your elbows. At the top, spread the rope ends apart slightly and fully extend your arms. Lower back down with control, feeling the deep stretch in your triceps at the bottom. The cable creates constant tension throughout the movement, and the overhead position really emphasizes the long head.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Dumbbell kickbacks are perfect for isolating your triceps and getting an incredible pump. Place your left hand and left knee on a bench for support. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and position your upper arm parallel to your torso - this is your locked position. Your elbow should be bent at 90 degrees. From here, straighten your arm by extending your elbow, kicking the dumbbell back behind you. The key is keeping your upper arm completely still - it stays glued to your side. Fully extend your arm and squeeze your tricep hard at the back. Control the weight back to the starting position. You won't use heavy weight on this exercise - it's all about that peak contraction and squeeze at the end. This is a perfect finisher exercise.

exercises.video_explanation_script: Reverse-grip pushdowns are a great variation that emphasizes the medial head of your triceps. Set up exactly like regular cable pushdowns with the pulley at the top, but here's the key difference: use an underhand grip with your palms facing up. Stand facing the machine with your elbows tucked at your sides. From here, push the bar straight down by extending your elbows, keeping your palms facing up the entire time. Fully extend your arms at the bottom and squeeze your triceps. Control the bar back up to chest level. The underhand grip feels different and specifically targets that medial head underneath your triceps. You might use slightly less weight than with an overhand grip, and that's normal. This is an excellent variation to include for complete tricep development.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The JM Press is an advanced hybrid exercise that combines elements of a skull crusher and close-grip press. Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell with a close grip over your upper chest. Lower the bar in a diagonal path toward your lower neck or upper chest area - not to your forehead like a skull crusher, and not straight down like a press. As you lower, your elbows move forward. The bar should lightly touch between your lower neck and upper chest. Press the bar back up following that same diagonal path until your arms are fully extended. This exercise allows you to use heavier loads than skull crushers while still isolating the triceps. It's named after powerlifter JM Blakley who used it to build massive triceps. Start light to learn the unique bar path before adding weight.
